REX_SERVER=unix:///Users/oleh.kotlinskiy/Library/Application%20Support/rex/server.sock

`REX_SESSION` identifies your session, and `REX_BLOCK` identifies your terminal
pane. Both variables are set in your shell. Pass `-s "$REX_SESSION"` and
`-b "$REX_BLOCK"` to select them in Rex commands. The user may be viewing a
different session or pane.

These inherited IDs haven't been checked against the server. If a target can't
be found, run `rex whoami --json` to check your current connection and location.

Use the `rex` command to create sessions, open tabs, split panes, run commands,
and read terminal output. In the CLI, a tab is a window and a pane is a block.
To run work on the user's other machines, use `rex hosts` and `rex -S HOST`.

The rex skill (/rex) provides instructions and
examples for Rex tasks. If the skill isn't installed, run `rex skill show` to
read the same guide.
